nodes.label: Circular Motion
nodes.note: Kinematics and dynamics of circular motion, vehicle turning, vertical loops, and spherical detachment. JEE tests centripetal force, banking, critical speeds, and the string-versus-rod distinction.

nodes.label: Circular Kinematics
nodes.note: Angular variables, linear-angular relations, and acceleration decomposition in circular motion.

nodes.label: Angular Variables
nodes.note: Angular velocity is $$\vec{\omega} = \frac{d\vec{\theta}}{dt}$$ and angular acceleration is $$\vec{\alpha} = \frac{d\vec{\omega}}{dt}$$. Infinitesimal angular displacement is a vector; finite angular displacement is not.

nodes.label: Linear-Angular Relations
nodes.note: Linear velocity is $$\vec{v} = \vec{\omega} \times \vec{r}$$ with magnitude $$v = \omega r$$. The total acceleration is $$\vec{a} = \vec{a}_t + \vec{a}_c$$.

nodes.label: Centripetal Acceleration
nodes.note: The radial component is $$a_c = \frac{v^2}{r} = \omega^2 r = v\omega$$, directed inward. It changes only the direction of velocity, not the speed.

nodes.label: Tangential Acceleration
nodes.note: The tangential component is $$a_t = \frac{dv}{dt} = \alpha r$$. It changes only the speed, not the direction. Net acceleration: $$a_{\text{net}} = \sqrt{a_c^2 + a_t^2}$$.

nodes.label: Relative Angular Velocity
nodes.note: The angular velocity of $$B$$ relative to $$A$$ is $$\omega_{B/A} = \frac{v_{B/A,\perp}}{r_{AB}}$$. A particle on a circle has half the angular speed about a point on the circumference compared to the center.

nodes.label: Uniform Circular Motion
nodes.note: In UCM, speed is constant: $$a_t = 0$$ and $$a_{\text{net}} = a_c = \frac{v^2}{r}$$. The acceleration is always perpendicular to velocity.

nodes.label: Non-Uniform Circular Motion
nodes.note: In NUCM, speed varies: $$a_t \ne 0$$ and $$a_{\text{net}} = \sqrt{a_c^2 + a_t^2}$$. The angle between net acceleration and tangent is $$\tan\psi = \frac{a_c}{a_t}$$.

nodes.label: Finite Angular Displacement
nodes.note: Finite angular displacement does not obey the commutative law: $$\Delta\theta_1 + \Delta\theta_2 \ne \Delta\theta_2 + \Delta\theta_1$$. Only infinitesimal angular displacement is a true vector.

nodes.label: Dynamics of Circular Motion
nodes.note: Centripetal force is the net real force along the inward normal. It is not an additional force.

nodes.label: Centripetal Force
nodes.note: The required centripetal force is $$F_c = ma_c = \frac{mv^2}{r} = m\omega^2 r$$. It must be supplied by real forces: tension, gravity, normal reaction, friction, or electrostatic attraction.

nodes.label: Centrifugal Force
nodes.note: In a rotating frame, the pseudo force is $$\vec{F}_{\text{cf}} = m\omega^2\vec{r}$$ directed radially outward. It exists only in non-inertial frames and has no reaction partner.

nodes.label: Conical Pendulum
nodes.note: A bob on a string of length $$L$$ rotating at angle $$\theta$$: $$T\cos\theta = mg$$ and $$T\sin\theta = m\omega^2 L\sin\theta$$. The angular speed is $$\omega = \sqrt{\frac{g}{L\cos\theta}} = \sqrt{\frac{g}{h}}$$.

nodes.label: Conical Pendulum Period
nodes.note: The period is $$T_p = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L\cos\theta}{g}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{h}{g}}$$ where $$h = L\cos\theta$$. String tension is $$T = \frac{mg}{\cos\theta}$$.

nodes.label: Centripetal Force Misconception
nodes.note: Centripetal force is not an extra force in the FBD. It is the name for the net real force along the radial direction: $$\sum \vec{F}_{\text{radial}} = \frac{mv^2}{r}$$.

nodes.label: Vehicle Turning and Banking
nodes.note: Turning on flat and banked roads, overturning, and rotor mechanics.

nodes.label: Unbanked Road
nodes.note: On a flat curve, friction supplies the centripetal force: $$\frac{mv^2}{r} \le \mu_s mg$$. The maximum speed is $$v_{\max} = \sqrt{\mu_s rg}$$.

nodes.label: Cyclist Leaning
nodes.note: A cyclist leans inward at angle $$\theta$$ with the vertical: $$\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{rg} \le \mu_s$$.

nodes.label: Frictionless Banked Road
nodes.note: On a banked road at angle $$\theta$$ with no friction: $$N\sin\theta = \frac{mv_0^2}{r}$$ and $$N\cos\theta = mg$$. The rated speed is $$v_0 = \sqrt{rg\tan\theta}$$.

nodes.label: Rough Banked Road
nodes.note: With friction on a banked road, the safe speed window is $$v_{\min} = \sqrt{rg\tan(\theta - \lambda)}$$ to $$v_{\max} = \sqrt{rg\tan(\theta + \lambda)}$$ where $$\lambda = \tan^{-1}\mu_s$$.

nodes.label: Parking on Bank
nodes.note: If $$\tan\theta \le \mu_s$$, a car can park stationary on the bank without sliding down, so $$v_{\min} = 0$$.

nodes.label: Overturning of Vehicles
nodes.note: For a four-wheeler with track width $$d$$ and COM height $$h$$: the overturning speed is $$v_{\text{overturn}} = \sqrt{\frac{grd}{2h}}$$. Skidding occurs first if $$\mu_s < \frac{d}{2h}$$.

nodes.label: Skidding vs Overturning
nodes.note: A vehicle skids before overturning if $$\mu_s < \frac{d}{2h}$$. It overturns before skidding if $$\mu_s > \frac{d}{2h}$$.

nodes.label: Rotor (Death Well)
nodes.note: A rider inside a vertical cylinder of radius $$R$$: normal reaction provides centripetal force and friction balances gravity. The minimum angular speed is $$\omega_{\min} = \sqrt{\frac{g}{\mu_s R}}$$.

nodes.label: Rotor Minimum Speed
nodes.note: The minimum linear speed in a rotor is $$v_{\min} = \sqrt{\frac{gR}{\mu_s}}$$.

nodes.label: Banking Angle
nodes.note: The banking angle is designed so that at the rated speed, no lateral friction is needed: $$\tan\theta = \frac{v_0^2}{rg}$$. This prevents tyre wear.

nodes.label: Vertical Circular Motion
nodes.note: String and rod vertical loops, critical speeds, and detachment from spherical surfaces.

nodes.label: String Vertical Loop
nodes.note: For a particle on a string of length $$R$$: tension at angle $$\theta$$ from the bottom is $$T(\theta) = \frac{mv^2}{R} + mg\cos\theta$$. Energy conservation gives $$v^2 = u^2 - 2gR(1-\cos\theta)$$.

nodes.label: Tension Difference Invariant
nodes.note: The tension difference between bottom and top is universal: $$T_L - T_T = 6mg$$, independent of launch speed.

nodes.label: Critical Looping Triad
nodes.note: For a string: $$v_L \ge \sqrt{5gR}$$ at the bottom, $$v_M \ge \sqrt{3gR}$$ at horizontal, $$v_T \ge \sqrt{gR}$$ at the top. Critical bottom tension is $$T_L = 6mg$$.

nodes.label: Three Motion Regimes
nodes.note: Based on launch speed $$u$$: oscillation ($$u \le \sqrt{2gR}$$), slacking with projectile flight ($$\sqrt{2gR} < u < \sqrt{5gR}$$), and complete loop ($$u \ge \sqrt{5gR}$$).

nodes.label: Oscillation Regime
nodes.note: For $$0 < u \le \sqrt{2gR}$$: velocity vanishes at $$\theta \le 90^\circ$$ where $$T = mg\cos\theta > 0$$. The body oscillates like a simple pendulum.

nodes.label: Slacking Regime
nodes.note: For $$\sqrt{2gR} < u < \sqrt{5gR}$$: tension vanishes in the upper semicircle while velocity is still non-zero. The particle leaves the circle and follows a parabola.

nodes.label: Complete Loop Regime
nodes.note: For $$u \ge \sqrt{5gR}$$: tension remains strictly positive throughout the entire circle. The body completes full circular revolution.

nodes.label: Rigid Rod Vertical Loop
nodes.note: A rigid rod can support compression, so it cannot slack. The looping condition is only $$v_T \ge 0$$, giving $$v_L \ge \sqrt{4gR} = 2\sqrt{gR}$$.

nodes.label: Rod Critical Triad
nodes.note: For a rigid rod: $$v_L \ge 2\sqrt{gR}$$ at the bottom, $$v_M \ge \sqrt{2gR}$$ at horizontal, $$v_T \ge 0$$ at the top.

nodes.label: Detachment from Sphere
nodes.note: A particle sliding from the top of a smooth sphere of radius $$R$$: $$N = mg(3\cos\theta - 2)$$. Detachment occurs at $$\cos\theta = \frac{2}{3}$$, so $$h = \frac{R}{3}$$ and $$v_{\text{detach}} = \sqrt{\frac{2gR}{3}}$$.

nodes.label: String Slacking
nodes.note: When tension reaches zero before velocity, the string slacks and the particle enters parabolic projectile motion. This occurs in the upper semicircle for $$\sqrt{2gR} < u < \sqrt{5gR}$$.

nodes.label: Energy Conservation in VCM
nodes.note: Mechanical energy is conserved in vertical circular motion: $$\frac{1}{2}mu^2 = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + mgR(1-\cos\theta)$$. This relates speed at any point to the launch speed.
